page.layout: One column of alphabetical index entries with page references at the right, cut off at the right edge. Above the entries: the letter I. Further down: the letter G, a large initial G with GABATA, and the entries under it.; One column of index lines; page numbers at the right edge, the left part cut off; the letters N and D stand at the top.; One column of index entries, set flush left, with page-number lines centred beneath some entries. The top line is a letter heading. The right edge of the column is cut off by the scan.; One column of right-aligned page-reference numbers, with a few cut-off words at the left edge of some lines. Nothing above or below the column.
page.notes: The right side of the column is cut off, so several page references end early (funderé, funiculus, gaudere, gazophylacium, gemelli, gemere). Those are left as far as they are visible. The readings "fulcum", "gammadæi" and "633.670.738" are doubtful. Some entries are grey or faint, notably Gallus and gallia. Left parts of the lines are missing, so the entries are only fragments. The first number of "350.663" is doubtful, and so is the last digit of "69[?]". The line "h 120" begins with a fragment of a word. The letters N and D at the top may be alphabetical index headings. The letter heading "E X." is uncertain in its first letter. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout (for example "strictus", "gestare", "gloriosus", "gibbosus").
